issues.claim: New Jersey's 2023 OEWS estimate for Maintenance and Repair Workers, General (SOC 49-9071) in the Middlesex-Monmouth-Ocean area is $52,326 per year median, roughly $25.16/hour
issues.problem: Misattributed. In the cited NJ LWD PDF (2023 OEWS, Middlesex-Monmouth-Ocean, by industry sector) $52,326 is the 50th-percentile annual wage for SOC 49-9071 in the Public Administration sector row, not the area-wide occupation estimate. Other sector rows on the same table give materially different figures (e.g. Manufacturing $60,608; Accommodation and Food Services $35,986; Other Services $45,656), so the number is a sector slice presented as the area figure. The $25.16/hour figure appears nowhere in the source; it is a derived division of the annual figure by 2,080 hours and is labelled neither as derived nor as an inference (the table shows percentiles, not a median hourly rate).
issues.fix: State it as 'the 2023 OEWS median annual wage for SOC 49-9071 in the Public Administration sector of the Middlesex-Monmouth-Ocean area, $52,326 (NJ LWD, June 2024)'; or use the sector figure that matches the target buyer (Manufacturing $60,608; Accommodation and Food Services $35,986) and mark the hourly conversion as an inference (annual / 2,080).

issues.claim: An ESP32-S3 + MPU6050 vibration node running FFT features and a K-Means anomaly detector reported 96.5% detection accuracy and about 300 ms end-to-end alert latency
issues.problem: Partly misattributed. The 300 ms latency is confirmed ('approximately 300 ms' from data collection to alert via Node-RED/Telegram), but 96.5% accuracy in the Springer paper is the accuracy of the TinyML/DNN state classifier (stopped / average speed / high speed), not of the K-Means anomaly detector, which the authors describe as a separate and complementary algorithm. The same entry's sample descriptor ('Laboratory bench setup, not a field deployment') also conflicts with the paper, which claims a real-world validation with 98% detection accuracy over 2 months of industrial operation.
issues.fix: Attribute 96.5% to the TinyML classifier (K-Means was a separate anomaly detector), and correct the sample description to 'bench plus a reported 2-month field validation; single study, no independent replication'.

issues.claim: Tractian separate CMMS product: from $60/user/month, billed annually, 5-user minimum

issues.fix: Replace with 'Unknown - custom quote' or cite the actual Tractian CMMS pricing page and verify the $60/seat, annual-billing and 5-seat minimum there.

issues.claim: Milesight UG65 US 915 MHz gateway at $690 one per site; Banner QM30VT2 at $320.00 Digi-Key single-unit list

issues.claim: MaintainX: average hour of unplanned downtime about $25,000, 29% aging equipment, 60% skilled-trade shortage - rated strength Medium
issues.problem: All three numbers are correct, but this is a vendor-published, self-reported survey of 1,165 respondents with no methodology shown on the press release. Under the rating rule that vendor-supplied outcome data must be Low, Medium overstates it, and the brief itself elsewhere treats vendor data (Parts Town, Emerson) as Low.
issues.fix: Downgrade to Low, and describe it as a vendor-run survey of MRO professionals (not a measured outcome at customer sites).

issues.claim: 1 in 3 foodservice customers experience unplanned equipment downtime every week (Parts Town, 2025)
issues.problem: Substance is correct, but the cited partstown.com page returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch, so the claim rests on the search-result summary of that page (which matches: ~1,800 respondents in 2025, refrigeration and fryers most frequent/disruptive). Not independently verified from the primary page in this pass.
issues.fix: Keep the claim but add a data_gaps note that the primary report page was blocked and the finding was read from search-indexed copy, or cite a trade-press report of the study.

issues.claim: Only 14% of surveyed SMEs used predictive maintenance (Wiley, IET Collaborative Intelligent Manufacturing, 2023)

issues.fix: Open the paper (or an accessible mirror) and quote the sentence carrying the 14%, or move the figure to data_gaps and drop it from the evidence list.

issues.claim: Emerson/Johns Manville case study: 44 hours downtime avoided, 50% longer MTBF, 43% fewer mechanical emergency maintenance events, 260% program ROI in six months
issues.problem: Numbers all confirmed exactly on the Emerson PDF, but the entry's year is given as 'undated' when the document carries a 2019 copyright (and describes a program started in early 2002), so 'undated' understates what the source shows.
issues.fix: Set year to '2019 document (program from 2002)' so readers can see the vintage of the result.
